        Idea:
Implement a professional AI animated sequence creator in the Reigh video editor. Add a Sequence tool beside the existing floating Text and Effect Layer tools. It should open a SequenceCreatorPanel for generating structured Remotion timeline sequence drafts from a user prompt plus optional selected/attached timeline assets. It should treat effects as wrappers and sequences as first-class timeline clips. It should use TimelineConfig.theme/theme_overrides when present but style/theme must be optional. It should generate trusted structured clipType+params drafts against existing registered themed sequence components first, preview them in Remotion, allow editing core params/timing/assets, then insert or replace a timeline clip. Store inserted sequences as normal timeline clips with clip.params and clip.hold; do not introduce shot-theme as source of truth. Reuse existing selected media/attachment patterns where practical, use existing timeline asset registry refs, add tests for insertion/data modeling/render path, and avoid arbitrary generated code by default.

        Idea:
Implement a professional AI animated sequence creator in the Reigh video editor. Add a Sequence tool beside the existing floating Text and Effect Layer tools. It should open a SequenceCreatorPanel for generating structured Remotion timeline sequence drafts from a user prompt plus optional selected/attached timeline assets. It should treat effects as wrappers and sequences as first-class timeline clips. It should use TimelineConfig.theme/theme_overrides when present but style/theme must be optional. parseErr.message : String(parseErr);\n+      logger.info(`[AI-GENERATE-SEQUENCE] extraction failed: ${parseMsg}`);\n+      await logger.flush();\n+      return jsonResponse({ error: parseMsg }, 422);\n+    }\n+\n+    const drafts = [];\n+    const invalidDrafts: Array<{ index: number; errors: SequenceDraftValidationError[] }> = [];\n+    rawDrafts.forEach((rawDraft, index) => {\n+      const validation = validateSequenceDraft(rawDraft, {\n+        allowedClipTypes,\n+        allowedAssetKeys,\n+      });\n+      if (validation.ok) {\n+        drafts.push(validation.draft);\n+      } else {\n+        invalidDrafts.push({ index, errors: validation.errors });\n+      }\n+    });\n+\n+    logger.info(`[AI-GENERATE-SEQUENCE] validated drafts=${drafts.length}, invalid=${invalidDrafts.length}`);\n+    await logger.flush();\n+    return jsonResponse({\n+      drafts,\n+      invalid_drafts: invalidDrafts,\n+      model: llmResponse.model,\n+    });\n+  } catch (err: unknown) {\n+    const message = toErrorMessage(err);\n+    console.error(\"[ai-generate-sequence] Error generating sequence:\", message);\n+    logger.info(`[AI-GENERATE-SEQUENCE] error: ${message}`);\n+    await logger.flush();\n+    return jsonResponse({ error: \"Internal server error\", details: message }, 500);\n+  }\n+});\n*** End Patch\n"
}

        Idea:
Implement a professional AI animated sequence creator in the Reigh video editor. Add a Sequence tool beside the existing floating Text and Effect Layer tools. It should open a SequenceCreatorPanel for generating structured Remotion timeline sequence drafts from a user prompt plus optional selected/attached timeline assets. It should treat effects as wrappers and sequences as first-class timeline clips. It should use TimelineConfig.theme/theme_overrides when present but style/theme must be optional. It should generate trusted structured clipType+params drafts against existing registered themed sequence components first, preview them in Remotion, allow editing core params/timing/assets, then insert or replace a timeline clip. Store inserted sequences as normal timeline clips with clip.params and clip.hold; do not introduce shot-theme as source of truth. Reuse existing selected media/attachment patterns where practical, use existing timeline asset registry refs, add tests for insertion/data modeling/render path, and avoid arbitrary generated code by default.
